title: Blue Eyed French Bulldog: Causes, Health Risks and Puppy Eye Color
description: Why a blue eyed French Bulldog has blue eyes (merle, white, puppy pigment), the links to deafness and eye defects, and when blue or cloudy eyes need a vet.
secondaryKeywords: do french bulldog eyes stay blue
do french bulldog puppies eyes change color

faq.q: Do French Bulldog eyes stay blue?
faq.a: In most puppies, no. Eyes often look blue when they first open and darken to brown as pigment develops. Eyes that are still clearly blue in an adult are usually genetic, most often from merle.

faq.q: Are blue eyed French Bulldogs healthy?
faq.a: Blue eyes alone are not painful, but they often come with merle or extensive white, which are linked to deafness and, in double merles, eye defects. Ask for merle DNA results, a BAER hearing test and an eye exam.

faq.q: Are blue eyed French Bulldogs deaf?
faq.a: Not all, but blue-eyed dogs are statistically more likely to be deaf because pigment-related deafness often comes with blue eyes and white coats. Only a BAER test checks each ear.

faq.q: Can a French Bulldog have one blue eye?
faq.a: Yes, usually from merle or white spotting. The FCI standard disqualifies eyes of two different colors, and Merck notes iris gaps (colobomas) are most common in multicolored eyes, so an eye exam is sensible.

faq.q: Why is my French Bulldog's eye turning blue or cloudy?
faq.a: In an adult, a new blue or cloudy look usually comes from the cornea, a cataract or glaucoma, not the iris. See a vet the same day, especially if the eye is red, painful or bulging.
